Multi-season models follow the same sites through several seasons, and ask how occupancy
changes between them. This vignette uses project 0010, shipped with WildObsR: 28 camera
stations in Woomargama National Park, New South Wales, that ran almost continuously for ten
months in 2021–22. It builds on *Detection histories and sampling effort* and *Fit
single-season models*.

## How WildObs splits a long survey

WildObs splits sampling into single-season surveys, its `deploymentGroups`, of at most 100
days, so each can be modelled as one closed season. `survey_and_deployment_generator()` is the
function that defines them from the timing of the records. Here it rebuilds 0010's surveys
from its observations:


``` r
# load the R package
library(WildObsR)

# grab the Woomargama survey shipped with WildObsR
dp <- example_datapackages("NSW_Woomargama_wombats_Linley_2021-22_WildObsID_0010")[[1]]
# extract the deployments and observations, read with their schema types
deps <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "deployments")
obs <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "observations")

# observations that can be placed on a camera, with each camera's landscape and project
caps <- obs[!grepl("^obscured_for_", obs$deploymentID), ]
caps <- merge(caps, deps[, c("deploymentID", "locationName")], by = "deploymentID")
caps$dataSource <- dp$name
# the function needs every deployment to have records, so keep those that do
deps_rec <- deps[deps$deploymentID %in% caps$deploymentID, ]

# group the records into surveys of at most 100 days
caps <- survey_and_deployment_generator(caps, deps_rec)
# look up the survey WildObs recorded for each record's deployment
recorded <- deps$deploymentGroups[match(caps$deploymentID, deps$deploymentID)]
# the records in each rebuilt survey, beside the survey WildObs recorded
table(rebuilt = caps$new_deploymentGroups, recorded = sub("_Linley.*", "", recorded))
#>                               recorded
#> rebuilt                        Woomargama_NP_2021_a Woomargama_NP_2021_b
#>   Woomargama_NP_2021_a_2021-22                 5246                    0
#>   Woomargama_NP_2021_b_2021-22                    0                 6383
#>   Woomargama_NP_2022_a_2021-22                    0                    0
#>   Woomargama_NP_2022_b_2021-22                    0                    0
#>                               recorded
#> rebuilt                        Woomargama_NP_2022_a Woomargama_NP_2022_b
#>   Woomargama_NP_2021_a_2021-22                    0                    0
#>   Woomargama_NP_2021_b_2021-22                    0                    0
#>   Woomargama_NP_2022_a_2021-22                 5138                    0
#>   Woomargama_NP_2022_b_2021-22                    0                  216
```

The rebuilt surveys match the four recorded ones. The data package already holds them, so you
rarely need to run this yourself. Each survey has its own dates in the metadata:


``` r
# the start and end of each survey, from the temporal metadata
blocks <- dp$temporal[grepl("WildObsID", names(dp$temporal))]
data.frame(survey = names(blocks), start = sapply(blocks, `[[`, "start"),
           end = sapply(blocks, `[[`, "end"), row.names = NULL)
#>                                       survey      start        end
#> 1 Woomargama_NP_2021_a_Linley_WildObsID_0010 2021-06-27 2021-10-05
#> 2 Woomargama_NP_2021_b_Linley_WildObsID_0010 2021-10-05 2022-01-13
#> 3 Woomargama_NP_2022_a_Linley_WildObsID_0010 2022-01-13 2022-04-23
#> 4 Woomargama_NP_2022_b_Linley_WildObsID_0010 2022-04-23 2022-04-28
```

The fourth survey lasted five days, so the seasons modelled here are the first three.

## Rebuild long-term deployments

Because surveys end at 100 days, a camera that ran for ten months appears as several
deployments. `recombine_deployment_groups()` joins them back into one deployment per camera
within each `multiSeason_deploymentGroup`, and keeps a crosswalk to the original pieces:


``` r
# one deployment per camera per multi-season group
dp_long <- recombine_deployment_groups(dp)
#> NSW_Woomargama_wombats_Linley_2021-22_WildObsID_0010: 94 obscured observations row(s) kept unchanged in recombine_deployment_groups(); they have no camera to join to.
# the rebuilt deployments, and the crosswalk to the original pieces
deps_long <- frictionless::read_resource(dp_long, "deployments")
crosswalk <- frictionless::read_resource(dp_long, "deployment_crosswalk")
# the observations, now pointing at the rebuilt deployments
obs_long <- frictionless::read_resource(dp_long, "observations")
# compare the number of deployments before and after
c(original = nrow(deps), rebuilt = nrow(deps_long))
#> original  rebuilt 
#>      219       57
```

## Effort on a shared calendar

A multi-season model needs occasion `k` to cover the same dates at every site, so
`align = "calendar"` starts every station's occasions on the first day of the project. The
crosswalk takes effort from the original pieces, so any gap between them counts as no effort.
Ten-day occasions over the first 300 days give ten occasions in each of the three seasons:


``` r
# camera-days per station and 10-day occasion, on one calendar for all stations
eff <- effort_matrix(deps_long, site_col = "locationID", w = 10, dur = 300,
                     align = "calendar", crosswalk = crosswalk,
                     time_zone = dp$temporal$timeZone)

# the start date of every occasion
occ_start <- unique(eff$occasions[, c("occasion", "start")])$start
# the survey each occasion starts in: the last survey that began on or before it
season <- vapply(occ_start, function(s) {
  # the surveys that had begun by this date
  begun <- vapply(blocks, function(b) as.Date(b$start) <= s, logical(1))
  # take the latest of them
  names(blocks)[max(which(begun))]
}, character(1))
# view how many occasions each season holds
table(season)
#> season
#> Woomargama_NP_2021_a_Linley_WildObsID_0010 
#>                                         10 
#> Woomargama_NP_2021_b_Linley_WildObsID_0010 
#>                                         10 
#> Woomargama_NP_2022_a_Linley_WildObsID_0010 
#>                                         10
```

## Colonisation and extinction in unmarked

The black rat (*Rattus rattus*), an introduced species, was detected at more of the stations in
each season. `colext()` estimates the occupancy of the first season, then the probability that
an empty station is colonised and that an occupied one goes extinct between seasons:


``` r
# create the detection history of black rats in each station and occasion
y_rat <- detection_matrix(obs_long, eff, "Rattus rattus")
#> detection_matrix(): set aside 94 obscured observation(s), which carry no camera.
#> Detection histories from public data under-count those species where they are listed.
#> detection_matrix(): left out 40 detection(s) after the first 300 days (dur).
# format it for unmarked, with the season of every occasion
umf <- model_matrix_input(y_rat, eff, seasons = season, output = "unmarked")
# view the number of stations, seasons and occasions in total
c(stations = unmarked::numSites(umf), seasons = umf@numPrimary, occasions = ncol(unmarked::getY(umf)))
#>  stations   seasons occasions 
#>        28         3        30
```


``` r
# load the unmarked package
library(unmarked)
# constant first-season occupancy, colonisation and extinction; detection rises with effort
rat_colext <- colext(psiformula = ~ 1, gammaformula = ~ 1, epsilonformula = ~ 1,
                     pformula = ~ scale(effort), data = umf)
rat_colext
#> 
#> Call:
#> colext(psiformula = ~1, gammaformula = ~1, epsilonformula = ~1, 
#>     pformula = ~scale(effort), data = umf)
#> 
#> Initial (logit-scale):
#>  Estimate    SE    z P(>|z|)
#>     0.291 0.383 0.76   0.447
#> 
#> Colonization (logit-scale):
#>  Estimate    SE     z P(>|z|)
#>     0.367 0.435 0.843   0.399
#> 
#> Extinction (logit-scale):
#>  Estimate    SE     z  P(>|z|)
#>     -1.55 0.454 -3.42 0.000636
#> 
#> Detection (logit-scale):
#>               Estimate     SE      z P(>|z|)
#> (Intercept)    -0.0738 0.0847 -0.871   0.384
#> scale(effort)  -0.0594 0.0836 -0.711   0.477
#> 
#> AIC: 892.9541 
#> Number of sites: 28

# the share of stations occupied in each season, for the population and for these 28 stations
rbind(population = rat_colext@projected.mean["occupied", ],
      these_stations = smoothed(rat_colext)["occupied", ])
#>                        1         2         3
#> population     0.5721569 0.7248353 0.7606075
#> these_stations 0.5721557 0.6445840 0.8220563
```

Occupancy rose from winter 2021 to summer 2022 because colonisation outweighed extinction.
Covariates go in each formula, just as in `occu()`.

## Occupancy over time in spOccupancy

`tPGOcc()` models occupancy in each season directly, here as a trend across the seasons,
rather than through colonisation and extinction. Its `y` is station x season x occasion:


``` r
# load the spOccupancy package
library(spOccupancy)
# format the detections for spOccupancy, with a season dimension
rat_sp <- model_matrix_input(y_rat, eff, seasons = season, output = "spOccupancy")
# view station x season x occasion
dim(rat_sp$y)
#> [1] 28  3 10

# the number of stations
n_station <- nrow(rat_sp$y)
# a station x season matrix of season numbers, for the trend in occupancy
rat_sp$occ.covs <- list(season = matrix(1:3, n_station, 3, byrow = TRUE))
# the season of every station, season and occasion, for detection
rat_sp$det.covs$season <- array(rep(1:3, each = n_station), dim = dim(rat_sp$y))
# number each station, for a random intercept in detection
rat_sp$det.covs$station <- seq_len(n_station)
```

Detection here differs among stations and among seasons, so detection has a random intercept
for each station and an effect for each season:


``` r
# make the chains repeatable
set.seed(1)
# a trend in occupancy across seasons; detection by effort, season and station
rat_t <- tPGOcc(occ.formula = ~ season,
                det.formula = ~ scale(effort) + factor(season) + (1 | station),
                data = rat_sp, n.batch = 600, batch.length = 25, n.burn = 5000,
                n.thin = 10, n.chains = 3, verbose = FALSE)
summary(rat_t)
#> 
#> Call:
#> tPGOcc(occ.formula = ~season, det.formula = ~scale(effort) + 
#>     factor(season) + (1 | station), data = rat_sp, n.batch = 600, 
#>     batch.length = 25, verbose = FALSE, n.burn = 5000, n.thin = 10, 
#>     n.chains = 3)
#> 
#> Samples per Chain: 15000
#> Burn-in: 5000
#> Thinning Rate: 10
#> Number of Chains: 3
#> Total Posterior Samples: 3000
#> Run Time (min): 0.1746
#> 
#> Occurrence (logit scale): 
#>               Mean     SD    2.5%    50%  97.5%   Rhat  ESS
#> (Intercept) 0.7426 1.2851 -1.6564 0.6910 3.5063 1.0039 2513
#> season      1.5611 1.0061  0.0013 1.4185 3.9448 1.0212  489
#> 
#> Detection (logit scale): 
#>                    Mean     SD    2.5%     50%   97.5%   Rhat  ESS
#> (Intercept)     -1.5143 0.4870 -2.4665 -1.5214 -0.5808 1.0073  639
#> scale(effort)   -0.0459 0.1065 -0.2576 -0.0470  0.1634 1.0016 3184
#> factor(season)2  0.1734 0.2843 -0.3750  0.1737  0.7198 1.0017 2827
#> factor(season)3  1.4211 0.2938  0.8656  1.4172  1.9874 1.0020 2466
#> 
#> Detection Random Effect Variances (logit scale): 
#>           Mean     SD   2.5%    50%   97.5%   Rhat  ESS
#> station 5.3901 2.0702 2.5394 5.0162 10.4357 1.0001 2091
```


``` r
# compare real and simulated detections, summed by station, then by occasion
summary(ppcOcc(rat_t, fit.stat = "freeman-tukey", group = 1))
#> Currently on time period 1 out of 3
#> Currently on time period 2 out of 3
#> Currently on time period 3 out of 3
#> 
#> Call:
#> ppcOcc(object = rat_t, fit.stat = "freeman-tukey", group = 1)
#> 
#> Samples per Chain: 15000
#> Burn-in: 5000
#> Thinning Rate: 10
#> Number of Chains: 3
#> Total Posterior Samples: 3000
#> 
#> ----------------------------------------
#> 	All time periods combined
#> ----------------------------------------
#> Bayesian p-value:  0.1436 
#> 
#> ----------------------------------------
#> 	Individual time periods
#> ----------------------------------------
#> Time Period 1 Bayesian p-value: 0.1073
#> Time Period 2 Bayesian p-value: 0.1053
#> Time Period 3 Bayesian p-value: 0.218
#> Fit statistic:  freeman-tukey
summary(ppcOcc(rat_t, fit.stat = "freeman-tukey", group = 2))
#> Currently on time period 1 out of 3
#> Currently on time period 2 out of 3
#> Currently on time period 3 out of 3
#> 
#> Call:
#> ppcOcc(object = rat_t, fit.stat = "freeman-tukey", group = 2)
#> 
#> Samples per Chain: 15000
#> Burn-in: 5000
#> Thinning Rate: 10
#> Number of Chains: 3
#> Total Posterior Samples: 3000
#> 
#> ----------------------------------------
#> 	All time periods combined
#> ----------------------------------------
#> Bayesian p-value:  0.2041 
#> 
#> ----------------------------------------
#> 	Individual time periods
#> ----------------------------------------
#> Time Period 1 Bayesian p-value: 0.2747
#> Time Period 2 Bayesian p-value: 0.3043
#> Time Period 3 Bayesian p-value: 0.0333
#> Fit statistic:  freeman-tukey
```

The chains converge and occupancy rises across the seasons, as `colext()` found. The
Bayesian p-values, though, fall below the 0.25 to 0.75 we treat as an adequate fit, so this
model still misses some of the variation in detection. Before trusting its estimates, try
detection covariates that change within a season, such as weather, or a random effect for
each station in each season. With 28 stations, simpler models may also suit the data better.
